title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short handwritten note in blue ink on the back of a recycled typescript page. The typescript is SGA 7, Exposé IX, pp. 110–111 (Lemme 9.4.3, Néron models / Kummer sequence). The typescript has nothing to do with the note. The note reads roughly: 'Hence the category of graded S-comodules is equivalent to the category of graded S^∨-modules C that are "locally nilpotent", i.e. such that for every x ∈ C the map u ↦ u·x from S^∨ to C is continuous for the topology induced on S^∨ (≅ the graded topology on ...)'.

In modern terms, S is a graded coalgebra over a base ring A. In the context of the 1976 lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex, S is most likely the symmetric coalgebra Sym(V) or the divided-power coalgebra Γ(V). S^∨ is its graded or complete dual algebra, for example the completed divided-power algebra or the power-series algebra dual to it. The statement is the standard duality between comodules and modules. A comodule over a coalgebra S is the same thing as a module over the dual algebra S^∨ that is 'rational' or 'discrete'. Equivalently, the action is continuous for the linear topology on S^∨ given by the orthogonals of finite pieces (the ideals S^∨_{≥n} in the graded case). Equivalently again, every element is killed by some power of the augmentation ideal, which is local nilpotence.

The purpose is presumably to translate structures on the divided-power de Rham complex (for example, the action of differential operators or the Cartier-type duality between Sym and Γ) into module language over the completed dual. This is the kind of identification that also underlies the description of crystals and stratifications as modules over the PD-differential-operator ring with a nilpotence or continuity condition.
errors: No mathematical error, but the statement needs hypotheses. It holds as stated when S is flat, or better locally free of finite type in each degree, over the base, so that S^∨ is a good dual. Over a general base ring the equivalence between comodules and rational modules can fail without such projectivity assumptions.
'qui soit' should be 'qui sont' (grammar of the note).

ideas.what: The category of (graded) comodules over a coalgebra S is equivalent to the category of discrete or locally nilpotent modules over the dual topological algebra S^∨, i.e. those with a continuous action.
ideas.modern_name: Comodule–rational-module duality (comodules over C = discrete modules over the pseudocompact algebra C*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard: Sweedler (Hopf Algebras, 1969); Gabriel (pseudocompact algebras, 1962); Cartier/Dieudonné for the Sym/Γ duality
ideas.where_published: Similar module/comodule identifications appear implicitly in SGA 3 (Exp. I, representations of affine groups as comodules) and in Berthelot's Cohomologie cristalline (stratifications vs. modules over PD-differential operators). It is unsure whether this exact statement appears in Grothendieck's own texts.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-known equivalence (comodules ≅ locally nilpotent or continuous modules over the dual algebra), jotted down as a working step. Nothing here is new or unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: '$S^h$' is very likely '$S^\vee$' (dual of S); the 'h' is a handwritten ∨.
'$S^k$' in the last line is likely also '$S^\vee$' (topology induced on S^∨).
'qui soit' should read 'qui sont' ('...gradués C qui sont "loc. nilpotents"'). The crossed-out word before 'nilpotents' is 'loc.' and the crossed-out word after C is 'tels'.
The final parenthesis '(≅ top. graduée sur h^A)' is uncertain. It probably says '(= top. graduée sur S^∨)' or refers to the dual over the base ring A; the '≅' may be '='.
The reading 'équivaut' is plausible; an alternative is 's'identifie'.
